_about: Cyclohexane (1) + acetic acid (2) + water (3): isobaric vapour-liquid-liquid equilibrium at 101.3 kPa, from Liu et al. (2013). Liquid I is the organic (cyclohexane-rich) liquid, liquid II the aqueous one. Rows as the ThermoML record stores them: T in K; in liquid II the mole fractions of water and of cyclohexane; in liquid I those of cyclohexane and of water; in the vapour those of water and of cyclohexane. Acetic acid is 1 minus the other two in each phase (not stored in the record).

source.citation: L. Liu, C. Cheng, X. Mu, H. Li, W. Tan, Isobaric vapor-liquid-liquid equilibrium for water + cyclohexane + acetic acid at 101.3 kPa, Fluid Phase Equilib. 350 (2013) 32-36
source.access: Journal article is subscription-only; the same data is public in the NIST TRC ThermoML Archive (NIST open license).
source.tables: ThermoML record, PureOrMixtureData 1 (acetic acid + cyclohexane + water; phases liquid mixture 2, gas, liquid mixture 1; 14 rows): v1 T; p1 water and p2 cyclohexane in liquid mixture 2; p3 cyclohexane and p4 water in liquid mixture 1; p5 water and p6 cyclohexane in the gas. The record also stores an uncertainty for most values (not transcribed). The table number in the article was not checked (article not open).

notes: Read with validation/python/thermoml_read.py 10.1016/j.fluid.2013.04.011 --set 1 on 2026-11-12, values as stored. The first row has no acetic acid: the binary heterogeneous azeotrope of water + cyclohexane (liquids recorded as pure water and pure cyclohexane). CHEPTA has no fitted acetic acid + cyclohexane pair, so the comparison (test/vlle-acid.test.js) is with Modified UNIFAC 2.0 (predicted). To be checked by a person against the record (AGENTS.md rule 4).
